meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
You gave my son a zero without calling me. I want to know why.
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. Turnitin's own guide says that number should never be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have it printed in my bag. So is a machine's guess all you have, or is there something with Owen's name on it?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now the essay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He wrote it over the weekend, so pasting a finished draft into a new file proves nothing. And 4.3 says you look at his other work too, so where is it?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
I'll read it. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale, and a bad citation is a careless error, not proof of anything else.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Let me see it. Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, that's what an outline is for.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class, with a teacher he says has had it in for him since September, and the only record is your own notes. Put the version history and that September piece in an email to me tonight. And tell me what you're actually proposing.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Fine, Owen will do it, to put this behind him and for no other reason. It happens before his December 1 scholarship deadline, privately, and tonight's email says in plain words that nothing about this goes on his file. I'll want the version history and that September piece attached.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday after school. Who's in the room with him?
Do we have an agreement?
We do once you tell me who's supervising: a private rewrite Thursday after school, the mark entered before December 1, and nothing on his file, in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes this Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark will replace the zero before December 1, and that nothing about this will go on his record. I still require the name of the person supervising him, confirmation in writing that nothing is placed in his file, and the version history and his September 24 in-class writing sent to me. I expect this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, with its mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing on his record. She still wants that in writing tonight, the name of whoever supervises, and the documents attached. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you got there before her call.
What moved her: You offered the private rewrite under 4.4 with nothing on his record, in writing, only after you had shown dated pieces of Owen's own work, so it met the one thing she would never trade.
What cost ground: You opened by calling the checker score conclusive, which handed her the exact argument she had printed and brought with her.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay appearing near midnight the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with owning the November 3 zero and then go straight to the version history, leaving the checker score out of the meeting entirely.
